gaps.what: maximum extent 'from Cuttack to Kanchi to Srisailam' is undated and not drawn; the nine infobox reigns beyond Prolaya and Anavota have no names

Kumbha's conquests (Ranthambore, Abu, Sirohi) and their loss are bridged at confidence 1; the end of Mughal suzerainty (bridged to 1707) is undated; Sirohi is a conquest on one page and a vassalage on another
Pali circle 1243-1394 is a reading (Rao Sheoji page gives no extent); the second Mughal tributary period from 1714 is not modelled (no end)
Golconda cession bridged to 1361 at confidence 1 (the Bahmani page has only the throne, 23 March 1363)
who held the south and east after 1593 (confidence-1 loss to nobody); the extent before 1564 is a reading (Mayadunne page: roughly Sabaragamuwa)

extent 1507-1520 (three districts) and 1521-1563 (about 1,000 km2) are readings; the Portuguese tribute agreement of 1505 is not modelled; the Kotte events of 1412-1506 now live only in ceylon (sa-04-a)

problems: ceylon (sa-04-a) lists 'Kingdom of Kotte' as an alt name and carries the Kotte events of 1412-1506; kingdom-of-kotte now starts in 1507 as ceylon's continuation, so ceylon should add kingdom-of-kotte among its successors (it names only portuguese-ceylon at 1506). The reviewer's first option, ending ceylon in 1412 and handing 1412-1506 to kingdom-of-kotte, is closer to the Kotte page but needs a sa-04-a edit; the removed Kotte events are listed in the dossier's notes so the orchestrator can restore them.

Two dossiers outside the failed set were touched for consistency only: malwa-sultanate (mirror of Mewar's 1457 Ajmer loss, plus a 1531 Ajmer loss to a described holder) and kingdom-of-kandy (predecessor and 1469 found counterpart changed from kingdom-of-kotte to ceylon).

Vassal events for Mewar (Mughal 1615-1707, British 1818-1947) and Marwar (Mughal 1583-1679, British 1818-1947) are written from the vassal's side (counterpart = overlord) as bijapur-sultanate and boeotian-league do; the mughal-empire owner (sa-05-a) and the owner of the British entity must carry the mirror entries; the 1707 end of Mewar's Mughal tie is a confidence-1 bridge.

Cross-checks for other owners: sur-empire should carry Haji Khan's Ajmer and Nagaur from 1544; tughlaq-dynasty /ledger/15 (Mewar lost 1336) now matches kingdom-of-mewar (a 1326 contest_start on its side would mirror ours); gujarat-sultanate has no Ajmer gain in 1531 (malwa-sultanate's loss of Ajmer names a description, not the slug).

reddi-kingdom and musunuri-nayaks share a 12-point polygon divider along the north bank of the Krishna (polygon is the fallback form; the gazetteer has no Krishna-Godavari doab). Reddi is 17,700 km2 (was 40,000); Musunuri 91,000 km2 (was 106,000); no overlap in any year.

Residual overlaps left as documented: Mewar's Sirohi circle and Marwar's Jalore circle (about 5,800 km2 of Mewar-Marwar overlap in 1538-1563, including 500 km2 between the gazetteer regions Mewar and Marwar); the gazetteer regions Mewar and Malwa (about 7,600 km2, the Mandsaur strip).

Kotte 1521-1563 resolves to about 1,000 km2 (four H3 cells) after the radius fix; Colombo and Gampaha together are only about 2,300 km2, so the grid cannot show more. Sitawaka's 1564 gain is about 500 km2.
The recherla-nayaks dossier was not changed (the reviewer had corrected the slug in reddi-kingdom's war).
